paragraphs.context: chest beat: repeated slapping of the chest with one
paragraphs.simple: Gorillas hit their chests with their hands to make a loud sound. It can be a warning to others, or it can just show excitement.

paragraphs.context: 9,855 days (example): While gorillas in the wild typically gauge
paragraphs.simple: Wild gorillas know time by the seasons and the food. Ivan has no seasons in his cage, so he counts the days one by one.

paragraphs.context: silverback (also, less frequently, grayboss): an adult male over
paragraphs.simple: A silverback is an adult male gorilla with silver hair on his back. He leads and protects his family group.

paragraphs.context: People call me the Freeway Gorilla. The Ape at
paragraphs.simple: People give Ivan big names for shows and signs. Exit 8 is the freeway exit near the mall where he lives.

paragraphs.context: The names are mine, but they’re not me. I
paragraphs.mainIdea: The names are not the real Ivan.
paragraphs.simple: Ivan says the names belong to him, but they do not show who he really is. He is just Ivan.

paragraphs.context: Humans waste words. They toss them like banana peels
paragraphs.simple: Ivan thinks people say too many words and do not care about them, the way they throw away banana peels.

paragraphs.context: I suppose you think gorillas can’t understand you. Of
paragraphs.mainIdea: Gorillas understand more than you think.
paragraphs.simple: Ivan speaks to the reader. He knows that people think gorillas cannot understand them, and he makes a little joke about it.

paragraphs.context: Try knuckle walking for an hour. You tell me
paragraphs.simple: Gorillas walk on their feet and on the backs of their fingers. Ivan asks you to try it and decide which way is more fun.

paragraphs.context: I’ve learned to understand human words over the years
paragraphs.simple: Ivan has learned what human words mean, but he still does not understand why humans act the way they do.

paragraphs.context: Humans speak too much. They chatter like chimps, crowding
paragraphs.simple: Ivan thinks people fill the world with noise, even when they have nothing to say.

paragraphs.context: I used to be a wild gorilla, and I
paragraphs.simple: Ivan lived wild in the jungle when he was little. He still looks like a wild gorilla.

paragraphs.context: I have a gorilla’s shy gaze, a gorilla’s sly
paragraphs.simple: Ivan has white fur on his back like a saddle. It shows that he is a silverback, an adult male. His shadow looks huge in the sun.

paragraphs.context: In my size humans see a test of themselves
paragraphs.mainIdea: People think Ivan wants to fight.
paragraphs.simple: Ivan is big, so people think he is angry or wants to fight. But he is really thinking about nice things, like the warm evening sun.

paragraphs.context: I’m mightier than any human, four hundred pounds of
paragraphs.simple: Ivan weighs about 180 kilograms and is stronger than any man. His body looks like a fighter's body.

paragraphs.context: My family tree spreads wide as well. I am
paragraphs.simple: Gorillas, chimpanzees, orangutans and humans are all "great apes". Long, long ago they had the same family.

background.note: Scientists say that humans and the other great apes came from the same animals millions of years ago.

paragraphs.context: I too find it hard to believe there is
paragraphs.mainIdea: Ivan makes a joke about humans.
paragraphs.simple: Ivan is also surprised that he is related to humans, who he thinks are rude, silly clowns.

paragraphs.context: I live in a human habitat called the Exit
paragraphs.simple: Ivan lives in a small shopping mall next to a big freeway. The mall has a circus show three times a day.

background.note: I-95 is a very long highway on the east coast of the United States.

paragraphs.context: At the Big Top Mall, a creaky-music carousel
paragraphs.simple: The mall has a merry-go-round, shops, animals, and a circus ring in the middle with seats around it.

paragraphs.context: My domain is at one end of the ring
paragraphs.simple: Ivan lives in the mall because he grew too big and strong to live with humans.

paragraphs.context: Stella’s domain is next to mine. Stella is an
paragraphs.simple: Stella the elephant and Bob the dog are Ivan's best friends.

paragraphs.context: My domain is made of thick glass and rusty
paragraphs.simple: Ivan calls each cage a "domain". His cage is glass, metal and cement. Other animals live in cages of bars, wood or wire.

paragraphs.context: Three of my walls are glass. One of them
paragraphs.simple: There is a small hole in one of Ivan's glass walls. He made it with a baseball bat that Mack gave him.

paragraphs.context: A jungle scene is painted on one of my
paragraphs.simple: Someone painted a jungle on Ivan's wall. It looks nice, but it is not real: the water does not move and the flowers do not smell.

paragraphs.context: I am lucky my domain has three windowed walls
paragraphs.simple: From his glass walls Ivan can see the whole mall and a little of the outside world, like the parking lot.

paragraphs.context: Beyond the lot is a freeway where cars stampede
paragraphs.simple: Cars rush past on the freeway like wild animals. A big sign calls them to stop at the mall.

paragraphs.context: The sign is faded, the colors bleeding, but I
paragraphs.simple: The old sign tells drivers to come to the mall and see "the One and Only Ivan".

paragraphs.context: Sadly, I cannot read, although I wish I could
paragraphs.simple: Ivan cannot read, but he thinks reading stories would help pass his long, empty days.

paragraphs.context: The freeway billboard has a drawing of Mack in
paragraphs.simple: The big sign shows Mack as a clown, Stella standing up, and an angry, wild-looking gorilla.

paragraphs.context: That animal is supposed to be me, but the
paragraphs.simple: The gorilla on the sign is meant to be Ivan, but Ivan says the picture is wrong, because he is never angry.

paragraphs.context: Anger is precious. A silverback uses anger to maintain
paragraphs.simple: A silverback gets angry only to keep his family safe and in order. Ivan's father beat his chest to warn others.

paragraphs.context: My neighbors here at the Big Top Mall know
paragraphs.simple: Ivan says, as a joke, that the other animals are clever because they can do tricks. "Educated" here is not meant seriously.

paragraphs.context: I used to have a neighbor, a sleek and
paragraphs.simple: Ivan once had a neighbor, a seal, who could keep a ball on her nose all day.

paragraphs.context: The seal was hungry one day, or bored, perhaps
paragraphs.simple: The seal ate one hundred coins that children threw in her pool. This is why the chapter after this is called "gone": she died.

paragraphs.context: Mack calls our show “The Littlest Big Top on
paragraphs.simple: Mack runs a small circus show three times a day. Mack dresses as a clown and rides a little bike.

paragraphs.context: I don’t do any tricks. Mack says it’s enough
paragraphs.simple: Ivan does not do tricks in the show. People come just to look at him.

paragraphs.context: Stella told me that some circuses move from town
paragraphs.simple: Stella says big circuses move from town to town and have people on ropes, lions and many elephants.

paragraphs.context: Our circus doesn’t migrate. We sit where we are
paragraphs.simple: The mall circus stays in one place, like an old animal that is too tired to go on.

paragraphs.context: After our show, humans forage through the stores. A
paragraphs.simple: Ivan explains stores as if they were new to him. People "forage" (look for food) in stores like animals in the forest.

paragraphs.context: All day, I watch humans scurry from store to
paragraphs.simple: Ivan sees people pass money back and forth. To him, paper money is just old, dry leaves.

paragraphs.context: They hunt frantically, stalking, pushing, grumbling. Then they leave
paragraphs.mainIdea: Shopping does not make people happy.
paragraphs.simple: People rush around and buy many things, but Ivan sees that the things never seem to be enough.

paragraphs.context: Humans are clever indeed. They spin pink clouds you
paragraphs.simple: Humans make wonderful things, like cotton candy ("pink clouds you can eat") and swimming pools ("flat waterfalls").

paragraphs.context: My life is flashing lights and pointing fingers and
paragraphs.simple: All day people look at Ivan, point at him, and press their hands on his glass.

paragraphs.context: The glass says you are this and we are
paragraphs.simple: The glass wall says that humans and Ivan are different and will always be apart.

paragraphs.context: Humans leave their fingerprints behind, sticky with candy, slick
paragraphs.simple: People leave dirty hand marks on the glass. Every night a tired man, George, cleans them off.

paragraphs.context: Sometimes I press my nose against the glass. My
paragraphs.simple: Ivan's nose leaves a mark on the glass. Every nose mark is different, like every person's fingerprint.

paragraphs.context: Here in my domain, I do not have much
paragraphs.simple: Ivan is bored in his cage. He jokes that throwing dried poop at people is fun only for a short time.

paragraphs.context: In my domain, I have a tire swing, a
paragraphs.simple: Ivan has very few things in his cage: a tire swing, a ball, a small pool and an old TV.

paragraphs.context: I have a stuffed toy gorilla, too. Julia, the
paragraphs.simple: Julia gave Ivan a toy gorilla. Julia is the daughter of George, the man who cleans the mall.

paragraphs.context: The gorilla has empty eyes and floppy limbs, but
paragraphs.mainIdea: Why the toy is called Not-Tag.
paragraphs.simple: Ivan sleeps with the toy every night. He calls it Not-Tag; later we learn that Tag was his twin sister.

paragraphs.context: Julia is ten years old. She has hair like
paragraphs.simple: Julia is ten. Ivan says they are both great apes and both artists.

paragraphs.context: It was Julia who gave me my first crayon
paragraphs.simple: Julia pushed a blue crayon and a piece of paper through the hole in Ivan's glass.

paragraphs.context: I knew what to do with it. I’d watched
paragraphs.simple: Ivan had watched Julia draw, so he knew what to do. The crayon made a blue line like a snake.

paragraphs.context: Julia’s drawings are wild with color and movement. She
paragraphs.simple: Julia draws things from her imagination, like smiling clouds and swimming cars.

paragraphs.context: My drawings seem pale and timid next to Julia’s
paragraphs.simple: Ivan can only draw real things from his cage, like an apple or a banana. He jokes that he often eats them first.

paragraphs.context: But even though I draw the same things over
paragraphs.simple: Ivan draws the same things again and again, but he is never bored. When he draws, he forgets everything else.

paragraphs.context: Humans don’t always seem to recognize what I’ve drawn
paragraphs.mainIdea: People do not understand his drawings.
paragraphs.simple: People cannot tell what Ivan has drawn. He draws a banana, and they think it is something else.

paragraphs.context: Mack soon realized that people will pay for a
paragraphs.simple: Mack found that people will pay for a gorilla's drawing. Ivan's pictures are sold in the gift shop.

paragraphs.context: Even as a baby, still clinging to my mother
paragraphs.simple: Even as a baby, Ivan saw pictures in clouds and stones.

paragraphs.context: I don’t remember much about my early life, but
paragraphs.simple: In the jungle, baby Ivan drew with mud on his mother's back. She did not mind.

paragraphs.context: I know what most humans think. They think gorillas
paragraphs.mainIdea: What people think gorillas cannot do.
paragraphs.simple: Many people think gorillas cannot imagine, remember the past or think about the future.

paragraphs.context: Come to think of it, I suppose they have
paragraphs.simple: Ivan agrees a little: he mostly thinks about what is happening now, not what could happen.

paragraphs.context: When the Big Top Mall was first built, it
paragraphs.simple: When the mall was new, many people came to see Ivan all day long.

paragraphs.context: Lately, a day might go by without a single
paragraphs.simple: Now some days nobody comes. Mack is worried about money and says Ivan is not cute anymore.

paragraphs.context: It’s true that some of my visitors don’t linger
paragraphs.simple: The few visitors look at Ivan quickly and leave. Some of them feel sorry for him.

paragraphs.context: Not long ago, a little boy stood before my
paragraphs.simple: A little boy cried and said Ivan must be the loneliest gorilla in the world.

paragraphs.context: It’s not so bad, I wanted to tell the
paragraphs.mainIdea: You can get used to anything.
paragraphs.simple: Ivan wanted to tell the boy that life is not so bad: with time, you can get used to almost anything. This shows how Ivan has accepted his sad life.

paragraphs.context: My visitors are often surprised when they see the
paragraphs.simple: People are surprised that Ivan has a TV and watches small people on the screen.

paragraphs.context: Sometimes I wonder, though: Isn’t the way they stare
paragraphs.simple: Ivan wonders: people stare at him in his small glass box. Isn't that just as strange as a gorilla watching TV?

paragraphs.context: I’ll watch anything, but I’m particularly fond of cartoons
paragraphs.simple: Ivan loves bright cartoons. He laughs when someone slips on a banana peel.

paragraphs.context: Bob, my dog friend, loves TV almost as much
paragraphs.simple: Bob likes to watch bowling and advertisements for cat food.

paragraphs.context: We also enjoy old Western movies. In a Western
paragraphs.simple: In Western films it is easy to see who is good and who is bad.

background.note: Westerns are films about cowboys in the American West in the 1800s. The good man often wears a white hat and the bad man a black hat.

paragraphs.context: Bob says Westerns are nothing like real life.
paragraphs.mainIdea: Real life is not like a Western.
paragraphs.simple: Bob says real life is not so simple; it is not always clear who is good and who is bad.

paragraphs.context: I have been in my domain for nine thousand
paragraphs.mainIdea: How long Ivan has been in his cage.
paragraphs.simple: Ivan has been in his cage for 9,855 days. That is about 27 years.

paragraphs.context: For a while, when I was young and foolish
paragraphs.simple: When he was young, Ivan thought he might be the only gorilla left in the world.

paragraphs.context: Then one night, after I watched a movie about
paragraphs.simple: One night, after a cowboy film, a TV program about wild animals came on.

paragraphs.context: Then I saw him. He was bit threadbare and
paragraphs.simple: On TV Ivan saw a wild gorilla. He jokes that the gorilla was not as handsome as he is.

paragraphs.context: As suddenly as he’d appeared, the gorilla vanished, and
paragraphs.simple: The gorilla was on the screen only for a moment. Then the show moved on to other animals.

paragraphs.context: All night I sat wondering about the gorilla I’d
paragraphs.simple: All night Ivan thought about the gorilla. Where did he live? Was there a female gorilla too?

paragraphs.context: Or was it just the two of us in
paragraphs.simple: Ivan wonders if there are just two gorillas in the world, each in his own box.

paragraphs.context: Stella says she is sure I will see another
paragraphs.simple: Stella is old and wise. She says Ivan will see a real gorilla one day, and he believes her.

paragraphs.context: Stella is a mountain. Next to her I am
paragraphs.simple: Stella is as big as a mountain next to Ivan, and Bob is tiny like a grain of sand.

paragraphs.context: Every night, when the stores close and the moon
paragraphs.simple: Every night, when the mall is closed, Stella and Ivan talk in the moonlight.

paragraphs.context: We don’t have much in common, but we have
paragraphs.simple: Stella and Ivan are both big and lonely, and both like yogurt raisins.

paragraphs.context: Sometimes Stella tells stories of her childhood, of leafy
paragraphs.simple: Stella tells stories of her young life in the forest. Elephants remember everything; Ivan does not.

paragraphs.context: She says, “It is quite a belly, my friend
paragraphs.simple: Stella says Ivan has a big belly, and Ivan says hers is big too. They tease each other as friends.

paragraphs.context: Stella used to perform in a large and famous
paragraphs.simple: Stella was in a famous circus. In the show she stands on her back legs while a dog jumps on her head.

paragraphs.context: If you are a circus elephant and you stand
paragraphs.simple: If Stella does the trick, she gets a treat. If not, she is hit with the claw-stick, a stick with a sharp metal hook.

paragraphs.context: Elephant hide is thick as bark on an ancient
paragraphs.simple: An elephant has very thick skin, but the claw-stick can still go into it easily.

paragraphs.context: Once Stella saw a trainer hit a bull elephant
paragraphs.simple: Stella once saw a man hit a male elephant with a claw-stick. The elephant was calm, but dangerous, like a snake.

paragraphs.context: The man flew, Stella said, like an ugly bird
paragraphs.simple: The elephant threw the man through the air. Stella never saw that elephant again.

paragraphs.context: Stella’s trunk is a miracle. She can pick up
paragraphs.simple: Stella can do many fine things with her trunk, like picking up one peanut or touching a sleeping keeper.

paragraphs.context: Her trunk is remarkable, but still it can’t unlatch
paragraphs.simple: Stella's trunk is clever, but it cannot open the door of her cage.

paragraphs.context: Circling Stella’s legs are long-ago scars from the
paragraphs.simple: Stella has old scars on her legs from the chains she wore when she was young. She calls them her "bracelets".

paragraphs.context: Stella’s foot never healed completely. She limps when she
paragraphs.simple: Stella hurt her foot long ago, and it never got completely better. She limps.

paragraphs.context: Last winter, Stella’s foot swelled to twice its normal
paragraphs.simple: Last winter Stella's foot got very big and she was sick for five days.

paragraphs.context: Even now, I’m not sure she’s completely better. She
paragraphs.simple: Ivan is not sure that Stella is really well, because she never says when something hurts.

paragraphs.context: At the Big Top Mall, no one bothers with
paragraphs.simple: At the mall, Stella is tied by a rope to the floor.

paragraphs.context: It’s been two days since anyone’s come to visit
paragraphs.simple: Nobody has come for two days. Mack says he is losing money very fast and may sell everything.

paragraphs.context: When Thelma, a blue and yellow macaw, demands “Kiss
paragraphs.simple: The parrot Thelma keeps saying "Kiss me". Mack throws a can at her. Thelma cannot fly, but she jumps away just in time.

paragraphs.context: I wonder if my visitors have grown tired of
paragraphs.simple: Ivan thinks people may be tired of him. Maybe he could learn a trick.

paragraphs.context: Humans do seem to enjoy watching me eat. Luckily
paragraphs.mainIdea: People like to watch Ivan eat.
paragraphs.simple: Ivan jokes that he is a very good eater.

paragraphs.context: I am going to try to eat more. Maybe
paragraphs.simple: Ivan decides to eat even more food so that more people will come to watch.

paragraphs.context: “Ivan,” he says, “trust me on this one: The
paragraphs.simple: Bob tells Ivan that eating more will not help. Then he checks Ivan's chin for food.

paragraphs.context: Bob is a stray, which means he does not
paragraphs.simple: Bob has no home or owner. He is so fast that nobody can catch him.

paragraphs.context: I’ve tried to share my food with Bob, but
paragraphs.simple: Bob does not want Ivan's food. He likes to find food himself.

paragraphs.context: Bob’s tail makes me dizzy and confused. It has
paragraphs.simple: Bob's tail moves in many ways, and each way shows a different feeling.

paragraphs.context: Bob used to have three brothers and two sisters
paragraphs.simple: When Bob was a few weeks old, people threw him and his brothers and sisters out of a truck onto the freeway.

paragraphs.context: His first night on the highway, Bob slept in
paragraphs.simple: Bob slept in a cold, wet ditch. In the morning he was so cold he could not move his legs.

paragraphs.context: The following night, Bob found the spot in the
paragraphs.simple: Bob came in through the hole in Ivan's glass. Ivan woke up with a little puppy sleeping on his belly.

paragraphs.context: It had been so long since I’d felt the
paragraphs.simple: Ivan had not felt the warmth of another animal for a very long time.

paragraphs.context: Once I asked Bob why he didn’t want a
paragraphs.simple: Ivan asked Bob why he does not want a home with people, since people love dogs.

paragraphs.context: “Everywhere is my home,” Bob answered. “I am a
paragraphs.simple: Bob says everywhere is his home. He is proud to be wild and free.

paragraphs.context: Bob said Snickers sleeps on a pink pillow in
paragraphs.mainIdea: Bob does not want Snickers's life.
paragraphs.simple: Snickers, the poodle in the show, sleeps on a pink pillow and eats meat from a can. Bob does not want that.

paragraphs.context: Mack gives me a fresh crayon, a yellow one
paragraphs.simple: Mack gives Ivan a crayon and paper and tells him to work.

background.note: Pablo Picasso (1881–1973) was a very famous Spanish painter. Mack calls Ivan "Picasso" as a joke.

paragraphs.context: I know I have lost my magic, so I
paragraphs.simple: Ivan thinks he has lost his "magic", so he tries to do his best.

paragraphs.context: I lean back, and Mack picks up the drawing
paragraphs.mainIdea: Mack does not care about the art.
paragraphs.simple: Mack calls the drawing a "scribble" (a careless drawing). He only counts how many are done.

paragraphs.context: I strut across my domain for them. I dangle
paragraphs.mainIdea: Ivan tries to please the visitors.
paragraphs.simple: Ivan walks proudly, swings and eats banana peels for the children.

paragraphs.context: The boy spits at my window. The girl throws
paragraphs.simple: The boy spits at the glass and the girl throws small stones.

paragraphs.context: I display my impressive teeth. I splash in my
paragraphs.simple: Ivan does everything he can think of to interest the visitors, even eating and eating.

paragraphs.context: Like the spit-pebble children, Julia is a child
paragraphs.simple: Ivan is not sure about human children, but Julia is different. It is not her fault that she is a child.

paragraphs.context: While her father, George, cleans the mall each night
paragraphs.simple: Every night George cleans the mall, and Julia chooses to sit next to Ivan's cage.

paragraphs.context: Sara, Julia’s mother, used to help clean the mall
paragraphs.simple: Julia's mother, Sara, used to help clean the mall, but she got sick. Julia wants to help, but her father tells her to do her homework.

paragraphs.context: Homework, I have discovered, involves a sharp pencil and
paragraphs.simple: Ivan sees homework as pencils, thick books and long, tired sighs.

paragraphs.context: I don’t know why people talk to me, but
paragraphs.simple: Many people tell Ivan things, maybe because they think he cannot understand.

paragraphs.context: Julia likes science and art. She doesn’t like Lila
paragraphs.simple: Julia likes science and art. A girl at school laughs at her old clothes, but Julia likes a boy who teases her in a friendly way.

paragraphs.context: Sometimes Julia draws me. I am an elegant fellow
paragraphs.simple: In Julia's pictures Ivan looks beautiful and calm, never angry like on the billboard.

paragraphs.context: She draws him flying across the page, a blur
paragraphs.simple: Julia draws Bob running fast and hiding behind things.

sentences.grammar: "But" joins two opposite ideas. "They’re" = they are.

you can stop feeling it is strange or bad
